value.body: A three-year postgraduate surgical degree (MS) in Otorhinolaryngology after MBBS. ENT surgeons treat ear, nose, throat and head-and-neck conditions — hearing loss, sinus disease, voice problems, tonsils and head-and-neck tumours — using medicines, microscopic and endoscopic surgery.

items.label: MS ENT seats
items.note: Karnataka has the most (~310); a further ~11 DLO diploma seats
items.source: NMC PG seat matrix 2026-27 (as reported by Medical Dialogues)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: MBBS with a completed internship and registration with NMC or a State Medical Council. Seats are allotted on NEET-PG rank: MCC counsels the All India Quota and central / deemed seats, and states counsel their own quota seats.

value.title: At a glance
items: Much of the work is outpatient care and planned surgery, alongside emergencies such as airway problems and nosebleeds.
Private practice is possible but needs equipment such as endoscopes and microscopes, and access to an operation theatre.
Further training options include fellowships (otology, rhinology, head and neck) and MCh Head and Neck Surgery.
Government posts include specialist medical officer and teaching faculty in medical colleges.
